title: Load glazed pots into a kiln with no piece touching another, a post or the wall
instruction: Load all five glazed pots standing upright into the kiln. Glaze fuses on contact, so leave at least 2 cm between any two pots and between a pot and a dark grey post, and at least 1.5 cm between a pot and the kiln wall.
context: Melted glaze welds whatever it touches, so a glaze firing is loaded with clear air around every piece; pots that touch each other, a shelf post or the wall are scrapped and can ruin the kiln furniture. The whole batch has to be planned to fit: these five pots don't fit in one row with the gaps. Done by: kiln operators, production potters, ceramic studio technicians.
setup: A mock kiln (grey-painted wood, an open-top box) is fixed to the table between the arms: inside 21 cm front to back, from 14 to 35 cm in front of the arm bases, and 33 cm side to side, centred on the midline between the arms. A tan kiln shelf, a 5 mm tan-painted wood board fixed to the table, covers its whole floor; the four grey walls are 2 cm thick and rise 6 cm above the shelf (6.5 cm above the table). Three fixed shelf posts (solid wooden dowels painted dark grey, 2 cm in diameter, 10 cm tall, screwed to the shelf) stand on the shelf: one on the midline 31 cm in front of the arm bases (its centre 4 cm from the back wall's inner face), and one in each front corner, centres 15 cm in front of the bases and 15.5 cm left and right of the midline, touching the front wall and the side wall. Five glazed stoneware pots, closed upright cylinders, stand on the table outside the kiln. In front of the left arm, 32 cm left of the midline: green (7 cm diameter, 9 cm tall, 350 g) 18 cm in front of the arm bases, and blue (6 cm, 8 cm tall, 280 g) 30 cm in front. In front of the right arm, 32 cm right of the midline: yellow (6 cm, 7 cm tall, 250 g) 17 cm in front, red (5 cm, 6 cm tall, 180 g) 26.5 cm in front, and purple (5 cm, 4.5 cm tall, 150 g) 35.5 cm in front. All positions are centres. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Each pot loaded cleanly earns 0.2: its bottom within 3 mm of the shelf top, its axis within 5 degrees of vertical (either end up: the pots are closed cylinders, the same at both ends), at least 15 mm between its side and every wall's inner face, at least 20 mm from every post and at least 20 mm from every other pot at its level. For an upright pot and a post, or two upright pots, the gap is measured from above: centre distance minus both radii (a post's radius is 10 mm). When the other pot is tilted more than 5 degrees or lying, the gap is the shortest distance between the two pots' actual surfaces (from a lying pot's end, side or rim). A pot counts as at another's level when their height ranges overlap or are within 2 mm (one resting on top counts; one held more than 2 mm above doesn't). A pot too close to another loses its credit, and so does the other. All five loaded: 1.0. The score is 0 overall if any pot with its centre inside the kiln's inner outline touches, closer than 2 mm surface to surface, another pot, a post (its side or its flat top) or a wall (its inner face or its top edge); this includes a pot standing on another pot or on a wall. Contact is measured between the actual surfaces: for a tilted or toppled pot, from its actual outline (its side, ends and rims), not its upright radius; for two upright pots side by side it is the centre distance minus both radii. To a wall it runs from the pot's outermost point to the wall's inner face, or, for a pot above the walls, to their top edge. A pot's bottom, top and outermost points are those of the actual cylinder: a pot of radius R and height H tilted t degrees has its bottom H/2 x cos t + R x sin t below its centre.
reset_notes: Lift the pots out and stand them on their tape marks: green and blue in front of the left arm, yellow, red and purple in front of the right arm. The kiln, its shelf and the three posts are screwed or clamped down and never move. Pots are judged where they stand at the end: a top-down photo with a ruler gives every gap.
fidelity: Approximate: the pots are solid rigid cylinders and nothing is fired; a gap under 2 mm stands in for glaze contact. The kiln is an unheated open box with one fixed shelf and three fixed posts, no lid or upper shelf. Every object has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), grippier than glazed ceramic. Real trials use a grey-painted wood mock kiln and unglazed or plastic stand-in pots of the same size and mass.
